notes: Round 1. Both tasks implemented: app/models/user_session.py (new UserSession table, deliberately not TenantMixin, exported from app/models/__init__.py in both fast-init and full branches), app/services/session_registry.py (new -- issue/login_and_register/is_active/touch/revoke/revoke_all_for_user/purge_expired, the single accessor per ADR 0008), app/_bootstrap/session_policy.py (existing idle-timeout before_request hook renamed _enforce_session_policy and extended to check session_registry.is_active(session.get('_sid')) before the idle check, fail-closed, reusing the existing exemption list and JSON/redirect response-shaping -- no second before_request hook added). All nine login_user(...) call sites replaced with session_registry.login_and_register(...) across app/_bootstrap/routes.py, app/modules/auth/sso_routes.py, app/modules/account/services/account_service.py, app/modules/account/routes/account_routes.py, app/modules/account/v2/routes/account_routes.py. Logout (all three paths -- account.logout, account_v2.logout, api_logout) now revokes via AccountService.logout(), which calls session_registry.revoke(session.get('_sid'), 'logout') before logout_user(). Task 02: AccountService.change_password/reset_password/set_password all revoke via a shared _revoke_other_sessions helper (change_password keeps the acting session via except_sid=session.get('_sid'); reset_password and set_password use except_sid=None); change_password now returns a 3-tuple (success, message, revoked_count) and both v2/non-v2 change-password routes flash the count, sourced from revoke_all_for_user's actual return value (fabricated-data rule) with a fallback warning message when revocation itself fails after the password commit succeeded. No admin-initiated password-reset/disable path exists in this codebase (searched, confirmed absent, not invented). Remember-me kept enabled (not disabled) -- the SSO/SAML remember=True call sites go through login_and_register the same as any login, so there is no fresh-remember-cookie-with-no-sid case to special-case. Tests: tests/test_session_invalidation.py (new, 11 cases covering both tasks) reproduces the exact pentest steps from brief.md as TestExploitReproduction::test_replayed_cookie_rejected_after_logout (form login) and test_replayed_cookie_rejected_after_json_logout (JSON login/logout, asserts the 401 body's code=='revoked' specifically, to prove the NEW registry check is what rejected it rather than Flask-Login's own unrelated unauthorized_handler -- catching a real test-authoring bug along the way, see result.md). Both pass, confirmed in clean runs, and both must fail on main (regression proof). 11/11 pass. Fail-closed enforcement required fixing the shared tests/conftest.py::login_as fixture (mints a UserSession row now) and mechanically patching 56 other test files that build a session by writing _user_id/_fresh directly -- new tests/_session_test_helpers.py::mint_test_sid is the shared helper. Two ThreadPoolExecutor-based concurrency tests (test_typed_arb_decision_routes.py, test_typed_arb_adr_model_routes.py) initially failed because their login helper ran in a worker thread with no Flask app context, so mint_test_sid silently returned None there and the fail-closed check correctly-but-wrongly rejected those in-test requests; fixed by giving mint_test_sid an optional app kwarg that pushes its own app_context when none is active (db_session's session-factory patch is process-wide, so this still resolves to the same wrapped, rolled-back connection). Both concurrency tests pass in isolation after the fix. Regression sweep (all against TEST_DATABASE_URL flask_test): tests/test_session_invalidation.py 11 passed (x2 runs); tests/test_qa100_security_hardening.py + test_tenant_isolation.py + test_gdpr_auth.py + test_dashboard_modes.py + test_ba_tenant_and_authz.py 79 passed 0 failed (after fixing TestF07SessionIdleTimeout::test_hook_is_registered's assertion for the renamed hook); test_air_gap_runtime.py + test_billing_access_control.py + test_qa100_security_hardening.py 51 passed 0 failed; the two typed-ARB concurrency tests 2 passed in isolation post-fix (an earlier combined run of both files reported 84 passed 2 failed, both now-fixed concurrency tests being the only failures). One pre-existing, unrelated failure not caused by this diff: app/modules/account/tests/test_account.py and test_account_v2.py fail to collect/connect when run standalone (missing 'app' pytest-flask fixture resolution + a hard-coded DATABASE_URL pointed at a DB named 'archie' that doesn't exist locally) -- reproducible on main, not touched by this diff, left as-is and called out rather than hidden. python scripts/verify.py --tag static: 48 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (css-build, pre-existing local-machine gap, no vendored Tailwind CLI) -- confirmed clean twice, including after fixing a genuine tenant-scoping finding on session_registry.py's two UserSession.query calls (tenant-scoping-ok comments added, matching the model's own not-TenantMixin docstring). python scripts/verify.py bare (full, DB-backed gates) was NOT completed this round: partway through the regression sweep the local portable Postgres instance (C:/Users/.../pgsql 12.4-1 Windows/pgsql) became unresponsive after I ran several pytest invocations concurrently in the background and then taskkill'd stray python.exe processes to recover contention, which took down the Postgres backend; every subsequent start attempt has gotten stuck in WAL redo with no progress for 10+ minutes despite multiple pg_ctl restart/start attempts (data is WAL-safe, no corruption expected, just needs time or a closer look at why redo isn't progressing on this machine).
